utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Brdjanin, can you follow in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you. Please take your chair. Ms. Sutherland? Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ann Sutherland assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. David Cunningham and assisted today by Mr. Aleksandar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you too. Announcements. I realised this morning when I was given a copy of the scheduling order that we've made a mistake. And a correction will be issued in due course in the course of today. We had stated in it that the Defence, that the Prosecution shall finish its case by Friday 1 August, 2003 and that stands, we also stated that the Defence shall file any motion pursuant to Rule 98 bis by Friday, 15 August, 2003, at the latest, and that stands and then we had also stated that the Prosecution shall file its response to such motion at the latest 14 days after the Defence motion is filed. That's a mistake. We had never meant not even originally when we had submitted to you the tentative programme that the Prosecution would have 14 days. The Prosecution will -- the corrigendum will be issued emphasising that -- or showing that the Prosecution shall file its response to such motion at the latest on the -- by Friday, the 22nd of August, 2003. So that's the position. And the corrigendum will be issued later on. Yes, witness. Ms. Sutherland, Ms. Korner had a copy of the schedule as it was planned before, until we had that what was expected to be a frank meeting in my chambers and the Prosecution had one week while the Defence had one month, one month for the preparation of the 98 bis and the Prosecution had one week and we are returning to that, one week. This was a mistake. I mean, it's -- someone misunderstood what we had in mind. Yes, good morning to you, sir. Welcome to this Tribunal again. Hope you had a good rest. We will continue with your testimony and hope to finish with you sometime this morning. May I ask you please to repeat your solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland, please try -- I ask for your cooperation to try and limit yourself to the time limit that we talked about yesterday. So as not to cause problems. I wouldn't like the next witness to stay here unnecessarily in The Hague over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir we have a lot to cover in the next hour. We have already lost 15 minutes this morning so in answering my questions, can you answer the question I ask you and then if I need any further details from you, I will ask further questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in relation to what you testified about yesterday, when you described the first beating in the gymnasium by the men and one woman from the Suha Rebra unit you said that once they pricked you with a knife and a couple of other times you said you were jabbed. Was your skin cut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Yes, I had cuts. It was quite a jab. I was bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How deep were the cuts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know. Perhaps a centimetre or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You described the second beating by the three or four men from Seselj's group you said you were beaten and an old man was also beaten. Do you recall the name of this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know his last name was Music but I can't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where did this beating take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened in a classroom in the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that when you were detained in the Jasenica school were you beaten on three occasions. You described for the Court the first two occasions. When was the other occasion you were mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was then, on those two occasions, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Before we adjourned yesterday, you testified that you were taken from Jasenica to the Petar Kocic school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where is that school located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petar Kocic school is in Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the town itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. On the outskirts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibits P2113.2, .3, .5 and .6?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking first at the photograph P2113.2, which is ERN number 0326-5857, sir, what is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a gymnasium in that school, in the Petar Kocic school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that was where you were detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. We were here for a while and then we were taken to some smaller rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next photograph, P2113.3, sir, what is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is something like the bathroom and I was -- I was here. I was exactly in that room later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Approximately how long did you spend in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent there about a month and a half.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next photograph, P2113.5, sir, what is shown in that photograph? You can use the pointer. And pointing on the machine to your right, place it on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the rooms, then this room where I -- where we were, and that's the bathroom. The guards were here, and this one was bigger.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What were in the room at the very end, the first room that you pointed to at the end of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over there, that's where those from Sanski Most were kept, those who were then killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Going back to the -- looking at the photograph, can you point in which direction the gymnasium was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, to the right, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next one, P2113.6. ERN number 0326-5866, what is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows the school and the gymnasium down there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you point, put the pointer where the gymnasium is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You're pointing now to the white building in the background of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the gymnasium where we were and closer to us is, in the forefront is the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour may we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, did you know any of the guards who were guarding you at the Petar Kocic school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some I did know. Others I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you name the ones that you did know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was Zdravko Narancic, Miroslav Desnica, Luka Desnica, some Todic, one Todic, and some others whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Taking first of all Zdravko Narancic, what did he do before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was sort of a driver and an employee, a worker in a company which was called the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Miroslav Desnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked for the Public Security Service in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What were the ethnicity of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were you ever taken for interrogation or questioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken -- they used to take me for interrogation downstairs to what is it called, the headquarters of the police where the headquarters of the prison was, and Petar Senic was the boss there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did he do before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I know that he changed jobs. I am not sure where he worked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The transcript says Petar Senic. Was that the name you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Pero Senic or Petar Senic, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know whether others were taken for interrogation, either on the school premises or at the guard headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know whether other people, other detainees, were taken for interrogation either on the school premises or at the guards' headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were you mistreated during your detention at the Petar Kocic school?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It seems the witness isn't receiving interpretation. I'll repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But first we make sure that he is receiving the interpretation. Can you hear now? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear you. That's why I am not saying anything. There is something wrong with my headphones. I can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Ms. Sutherland, bear with us, please. Let's fix this first. And then we proceed. You still can't -- if the interpreter in B/C/S could say something so that we can in the meantime check? Thank you, usher. Can you hear me now? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not me directly but are you receiving the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Thank you, usher. Thank you, the interpreters. Ms. Sutherland you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, during your detention at the Petar Kocic school, were you mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were mistreated, all of us were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How many times in your -- in relation to yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in that position twice. I can describe that. I was electroshocked. They attached electricity to my feet, to my leg joints, and to my hands. Some people even had electricity attached to their ears, to their ear lobes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to go through this with you in detail. Do you recall when this first occurred? On the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember. The first time it was when all of us were there. Before the exchange, everybody had to go through that. Everybody had that sort of mistreatment done to them involving electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where did this mistreatment take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the small room where the guards, the police, stayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who administered this electroshock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boro Beslac was there and also Miroslav Desnica and this person whose last name is Todic and whose first name I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Boro Beslac what was his ethnicity and what --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is his name Djuro Beslac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Djuro Beslac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know what he did before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Todic, you said you don't know his first name. Do you know what his ethnicity is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a Serb and he is a native of Zenica. He served in the army in Croatia, somewhere around Glina. After his compulsory service, he was sent to Krupa to join the police there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court exactly what happened, the circumstances, where you were brought from, where you were taken and how it actually occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about this mistreatment involving electricity? This happened in those rooms and we went in those rooms, one by one, and each and every one of us had those clamps attached to our fingers and toes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How long did it last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five or six minutes or ten minutes, for everyone of us. It depended.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you describe the implement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a box car or a car battery. There were some wires and there was some sort of an implement with a handle that once you turned that handle, you would start the electricity running through that box battery, through those wires.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When they started turning the handle, what was happening then? What were you experiencing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was terrible. It was -- it was almost to die of. It was a very powerful electricity. I didn't die but I had a terrible time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How many times did they perform this electroshock on you on that first occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you mean when you say how many times?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How many times did they turn this handle? How many shocks did they give you on this first occasion that you went into this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times. They turned as many times as they wanted. Then they stopped. I didn't count but in any case, they turned the handle quite a few times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And on that first occasion, where were the clamps attached? Were they attached to your fingers and your toes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the room where the police stayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were the clamps attached to your fingers and your toes on that first occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they would attach them to the toes, once they were done with the toes, they would move the clamps to the fingers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When you first entered the room, was anything said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They just jokingly said, "Okay. Let's sing. Let's start singing."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And did you have to sing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't mean singing. That meant screaming in terror, but they called it singing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's an expression. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And were you screaming from terror from this experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, I think you can -- you have the authorisation of the Tribunal to spare the witness any more details on this particular part of the event.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, did this same electroshock -- did you have to undergo it on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had to undergo it two times. We all had to undergo it two times, but some people had clamps attached to their ear lobes, behind their ears, on that second occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour can we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, on both these occasions that you were electroshocked, were you intimidated by these experiences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left my ear drums. I am hard of hearing. I now suffer from frequent headaches, and that is what I can tell you. That's what I suffer from.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was this a humiliating experience for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was. Any normal person would never forget something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to turn now to another topic. Do you know of other detainees who were beaten or mistreated apart from this electroshock treatment during their detention in the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know some.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who do you know that was mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirsad Budimlic and Suad Sefic were beaten up quite a lot. And they would be swollen from beating, every 15 days they would be beaten and finally, one of them was killed and the other one was poisoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Which one was killed and which one was poisoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirsad Budimlic was killed and Suad Sefic was poisoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you just tell the Court very briefly how Suad Sefic came to be poisoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had to be killed. There was a military court in Zenica which decided that. They had to do it and finally they gave him poison. They gave him poison for two or three days and finally he died from poisoning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who gave him the poison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards, the police that was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you describe very, very briefly for the Court how Mirsad Budimlic was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you describe very, very briefly for the Court how Mirsad Budimlic was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mirsad Budimlic was beaten up quite heavily and sustained a lot of injuries and those injuries were all infected and there were maggots in those wounds and one day we asked the guards to call a doctor, the guard said that he would see to that. The following day, allegedly, a doctor came but it was not a doctor. It was the prison warden, Petar Senic, and Mirko Jasdic [phoen] the commander of the police platoon who came, and the guard, the policeman who was there was Zdravko Narancic, he came into the room and to our room and asked the four of to us carry Budimlic into the room where the police were. The four of us took him there, they told him to leave him there, and to go back to their room and they also told them when we are done with him, you will be called to pick him up. After some five minutes, they called the four men to come for Mirsad, a doctor was not there. Mirsad was just beaten up. And the only thing that we could hear in our room was him screaming, "What are my children going to do?" And some two or three minutes later, he died of his wounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to turn now to another topic. Were you ever taken for forced labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had to go to -- up to there Hum, to the hill above the school. Up there, there was a squad, and its commander was Milorad Kotur, up there they had some guns, some cannons, they had sharp shooters up there, and we were taken up there to dig some trenches leading up to the gun which was some 80 metres away from the house where they stayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was anyone killed during forced labour on the hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Three men were killed on the hill. One of them was Lieutenant Colonel Semovic -- Zijad Selimovic, then Muratif Alic, and Albin Bajrambasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to Lieutenant Colonel Zijad Selimovic, can you describe very briefly for the Court how he came to be killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Lieutenant Colonel was asked to fire from a cannon gun, and allegedly, he was killed by the BH Army that was shooting from the other side. His brother-in-law [As interpreted] was nearby and saw that one of Kotur's men actually shot at him and killed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you see his -- what happened with his body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His body was brought downhill to the gymnasium and on the following day, we took him to the cemetery in Lipik and buried him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know the name of his son-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nusret Malkoc.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the transcript says brother-in-law. Was it brother-in-law or son-in-law?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to ask you to point that out to the witness because the transcript says brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was his son-in-law, because his daughter was married to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is he still alive today, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. None of them are alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can go direct here or I do it myself. In one of your statements, sir, while -- when you were describing the killing of Colonel -- Lieutenant Colonel Zijad Selimovic, you said, "I did not see this happen but Selimovic's son-in-law did," which you have confirmed to us now. Then you said in that statement to the Prosecutor, to the investigator of the Prosecutor, he later disappeared. Who disappeared? This son-in-law disappeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He disappeared later on, when we went to Drvar. That's when he disappeared, Nusret disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nusret Malkoc disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, you also mentioned Muratif Alic was killed on the hill.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was also killed. He worked and I suppose he wanted to go to the toilet behind the house in the orchard, and I -- we thought that he also was killed by Kotur's guards because there was no evidence whatsoever that he may have been killed from the other side, by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you see his body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We buried him up there on the hill. Actually no, it was in -- on the cemetery in Lipik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you see any bullet wounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were two bullet wounds. One in the chest and the other one a bit lower.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I didn't ask you but did you see any bullet wounds on the body of Lieutenant Colonel Zijad Selimovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one wound. He had a helmet and there was this wound above the eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned also Bajrambasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How was he killed during forced labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly, he went up there alone to clean the rooms where they slept. Some half an hour later, one of the guards came to fetch us and he said, "Go up there to take Albin's body." He had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you notice any bullet wounds on his body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw holes in his clothes, in the back and in the chest.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, we are now back in open session. I just want to remind you of that. Do you recall any persons -- sorry, you mentioned earlier that there were a number of people killed in the room at the end of the corridor in the Petar Kocic school. Do you recall the names of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember their first names but I do remember their last names.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court their last names and the circumstances in -- as to how they came to be killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were seven of those lads from Okrec, from these Sanski Most municipality, who were called Kaltak. Three of them came from the village of Jasenica. One was called Nasic and the last name of the other two was Alijagic and there was also Teufik Sedic but he was in a different room. He wasn't with them in the room but he was killed at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was responsible for the killing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The responsible, I think, was some reserve Captain First Class, Jojo Plavanjac who worked at the TO headquarters in Bosanska Krupa before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for the Court the circumstances and how these men came to be killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly -- I didn't see him, but allegedly there was a Serb in prison who had allegedly killed that Jojo's mother and that Jojo had come to kill that Serb but didn't find him and then he heard that those boys from Okrec had come there, who had been trying to cross into the Cazin region but failed, returned home, were captured and brought to Bosanska Krupa so that that day, Jojo turned up and killed them all in that room in which they were, from an automatic rifle. And after he had killed them, from the room which was to the right were prisoners from Jasenica and Potkalinje were, Potkalinje and Dubovik were, there were eight of them, and that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this Jojo Plavanjac still alive, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where does he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, he's fled and he's somewhere around Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned that Teufik Sedic was in a different room but he was killed at the same time. Can you just briefly tell the Court the circumstances of his death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Allegedly, when Martic was captured in Bosanska Otoka, Jojo happened to pass through the village of Jasenica where Teufik was living, and there was Jojo's uncle and he allegedly teased that or provoked Jojo's uncle saying, "What are you doing here?" See, Martic had to be arrested, had to be caught, allegedly he provoked his uncle and that is why he took him out and killed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court how owe was killed in the Petar Kocic school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he quite simply came into the room where he was, took him out to the gym and killed him. That's all I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the bodies of those others that were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 minutes or half an hour later, a truck came up, which was used to carry the cattle from the cooperative that took them but that was late in the afternoon. It was almost dark. And later on, I heard from some that allegedly there had been taken to the cemetery at Lipik but I don't know anything else about them. This is all that I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have with the Court's indulgence, another ten minutes and I was wondering whether, with the interpreter's indulgence also we could have a bit of a shorter break at 10.30 in order that I can continue with the witness for another ten minutes? Bearing in mind that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham, let's organise it better. Having heard the witness now and expecting another ten minutes of direct, how long do you think your cross will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Probably 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We certainly can continue the next 15 minutes because it's 10.15 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But instead of having a 25 minute break can we have a 15 minute break with the Court's and the interpreters' indulgence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreters and the technicians have heard that. As far as we are concerned we have no problem. For sure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, Your Honour, I would ask that we have the normal break and here is why. Because of the limitations on our time to visit in detention because we are in trial, it is during the breaks that I have the most opportunity to speak to the accused. And it's important for us to have these conversations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's do it. That's fair enough, Mr. Cunningham. Let's do it this way. We will break at 10.30 for the usual 25 minutes but if you manage to finish your consultations with your client earlier, could you please alert Ms. Sutherland, the Registry and -- Registrar and all the others so that we reconvene as quickly as we can? And if we can gain five minutes, it's always better.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fair, Your Honour, we will be glad to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that fine with you, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, we have a lot to cover in the next 15 minutes. During -- you said that you were detained in the Petar Kocic school until the 21st of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where were you transferred from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of August, two army trucks came for -- carrying ten people each and we were 20 and they first blindfolded us, without saying anything, we were put into these trucks and on the 21st of August, we were taken to the camp in Kamenica. Many people had been beaten and suffered very many injuries on the way, so that this Kemal Sepic succumbed in Drvar. That is he arrived in Drvar but he was dead in the morning, and when we arrived in Kamenica, next to Drvar, as they were taking those tapes from our eyes, as they would come up to everyone of us to take off this adhesive tape from our eyes, they would also hit us with a baton and so we were put in Kamenica and were there until the 3rd of November. Funny things went on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of the people who were detained in Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kamenica, they were all Muslims except as far as I know there was also one Croat with us, but then there were on the other side some Serbs, some 40 of them, who allegedly had refused to go to war. And so they had been captured and put them in prison. They put them in the school in Kamenica. I know that. But where we were, we were all Muslims and one Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were detained in Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with us, who had come from Krupa, I'd say we were about 70.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In total, the number of people between the 21st of August and the 3rd of November, approximately how many people were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The total number I've told you, about 70, because two arrived subsequently, so around 70, because I know because of the exchange when we went to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misheard. I thought you said 17, not 70. I'm sorry, I apologise. Can you please tell the Court what municipalities these people were from that were detained in Kamenica, where they had come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were from Kljuc, the so-called Sanica, some others were from Petrovac, Bosanski Petrovac, some came from Kulen Vakuf, then from Cukovi, from Orasac, these places near Vakuf and we came from Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You weren't interrogated during your time in Kamenica, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And neither were you mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some yes, but I wasn't, no, not in Kamenica, no problems there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned that you weren't mistreated but some others were. How often did this mistreatment occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost every evening, they would take out men to sing and after they would finish singing they would be beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What sort of songs did they have to sing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly some Serb songs or something. I could hear that they had been singing and allegedly they were mostly Serb songs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you have to do any forced labour at Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were engaged in forced labour. It was autumn so we had to prepare firewood, to dig trenches, to make a fence around the camp. Some went to Drvar to bring some foodstuffs from upper floors to lower floors. I don't know exactly, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that a number of detainees went missing from the camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those four from Bosanska Krupa went missing, plus four of those who were there before us. So eight of them. And Dedic went directly to Bihac and we -- and 61 of us were exchanged and went to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think you've named three of the four people from Bosanska Krupa who went missing. Fehim Kadic, Nusret Malkoc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, about Sepic. His whereabouts are known.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was the other person that was -- went missing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't understand what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ferid Velagic, did he disappear from Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, Ferid Velagic, Fehim Kadic, Malkoc and that Sepic who was killed. But Malkoc and Sepic were found and taken to a grave in Bosanska Krupa. But about Fehim and the other one, Ferhid, nothing is known about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did the ICRC visit the camp and arrange your -- for you to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you said that you left the camp on the 3rd of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just very briefly, the guards that were at Kamenica, do you know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were two groups which provided the guards. One came from Petrovac and the other one came from Drvar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have two other matters that I want to ask you about very quickly. The first one is the destruction of religious buildings in Bosanska Krupa. Are you aware of any buildings that were damaged or destroyed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Religious buildings we are talking of for the time being, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mosques, churches or any other places of worship.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the town in Bosanska Krupa, there was a mosque, there was a Serb church and there was a Catholic church there, and during the war, the mosque and the Catholic church were destroyed, and of course mosques in villages, I mean in Muslim villages, all those mosques were destroyed. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How did you become aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew in the town, we just saw it, and later on, some groups went to work in villages, that is to bury the life stock which had died and when they came back, they said it's all been destroyed up there, villages and all that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you do -- did you have to attend any of the religious buildings on forced labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What about other property in the town of Bosanska Krupa? What other property was damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, by and large all the Muslim houses were either torched or destroyed, allegedly there were very few left intact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour can we go into private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session, Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would appreciate if everyone is possibly here in 20 minutes' time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cunningham, who is defending Mr. Brdjanin, will be asking you some questions. Your obligation under the rules of this Tribunal is to answer all his questions as fully and as truthfully as possible. Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I proceed could I point out what has been pointed out to me as two discrepancies in the translations? On page 7, line 22, the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because we will have to go to page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Line 22. It has been reported to me that the witness answered, the military police, but I believe in the transcript it only says police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the transcript it says police, the guards, the police who kept the guard. Okay. Let me -- this is with reference -- do you remember that sketch that you had -- that you had drawn and that Ms. Sutherland was asking you about? If we need -- in it, there is one room where you refer to it as POL. And you said that that was the room where the police were. In -- when you were describing this, did you say the military police or just the ordinary civilian police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't know. A policeman is guards, I don't know. It looks like military police but different thing whether it's military police or one word police, to me, everything is the same, police or the military police, civilian or military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You heard that, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think that clarifies it, Your Honour. The second one is this, and I apologise, I don't have the specific page number and line number. I do have the time number. The time number is at 9.59.39 and this is having to do with the timing of certain deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I have yet -- one of the things I have yet to figure out since I've been here is how to work LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think the witness said mid-July rather than mid-May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 9.59, 31 to 40, we have nothing like that, it says about 15 minutes half an hour later a truck came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Then I stand corrected, Your Honour. I will see it I can search it with the help of our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I can help you there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 20 line 2. What month all these killings took place between mid-May and mid-July and you say that the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Said what?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think the discrepancy is -- hold on a second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are talking, Witness, about Albin Bajrambasic and others that were killed at the same time. When did this happen? Which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that the killings were being committed between mid-June and mid-August.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours and with the court's permission, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I want to get you out of here as quickly as I can so that you can return home and the easiest way for that to happen is for to you listen carefully to my questions and try to answer them as precisely, as concisely as you can. Can you do that? When I read your statement, there is a passage in your statement that says -- and by the way, do you have your written statements that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor? Do you have that statement available in case you need to look at it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's give him the copy of the statement straight away and Ms. Sutherland, regarding that sketch that we referred to earlier, do you intend to tender it in as an exhibit or not? Because if you do, we need to have it under seal and numbered.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I thought the sketch was P2028. That was provisionally marked and I intended --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So please make sure that it is under seal. Because it bears the initials of the witness. All right? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: To assist the usher, Judge, the first statement is going to be the statement provided 26 August, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sir, if you could look at -- on your statement of 26 August, 1999, B/C/S version, at the third paragraph from the top. In that third paragraph from the top, you say, "I am not very familiar with the political situation before the war." Do you see that? It is on the first page of text, which is page 2 of the statement, third paragraph on page 2 of his B/C/S statement. Do you see that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it that you were not really paying that much attention to the political situation in your municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you about certain events that may or may not have been a source of conflict between the SDA and the SDS and I want to ask you if you knew anything about them. My first question is this: Did you know anything about the political dispute involving the removal of files from the National Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did you know anything about the political dispute between the two parties over the fact that some Serb municipal workers had been demoted or lost their jobs as a result of the election? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something that I heard about, and that's how it was, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: All right. And what did you hear about it, very, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard that the SDA party held the largest number of offices in the municipality, that the SDS had less offices, and that's about it. I wasn't really interested to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. Were you aware of any dispute between the SDS in the municipal administration about the Branko Copic monument? Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's another thing that I heard about, but allegedly there was no need to put up another monument seeing that there was already a monument of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Is that about all you know about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fair. Did you know anything?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about an incident between the local police that happened in Arapusa where two -- where some Serbs were shot by the police? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that but I simply paid no attention because that was none of my business and there were other people who dealt with it. I mean people who were concerned with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just answer the question. The question was whether you heard about it. It's not whether you were worried about it or whether you had personal opinions and what, just answer yes or no, all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. My next question is: Did you know anything about when Serbian police officers in the local police left the police department and moved to Jasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Was -- do you know, and this is like His Honour told you, Mr. President told you, that this is a question that calls for yes or no. Did you know whether or not, when the Serb police officers left, whether that was a source of dispute between the two parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The final area I want to talk to you about is: Did you become aware of the incident in September of 1991 involving Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Remember we are in open session so I don't want you to tell me the street name or anything like that, but I believe you told us in your statements that you lived in a village that had both Serbian and Muslim households.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: All right. Did you live in an all-Muslim neighbourhood, an all-Serb neighbourhood or a mixed neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what villages do you mean and what do you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Maybe we should go in private session just to clear this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are in open session and you may proceed, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The neighbourhood in which you lived was an area patrolled by the police, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes, but the police patrolled all over the town, not only there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You told us yesterday -- you told us in your testimony that you saw on at least one occasion individuals taking weapons into their basement at a Serb house. My question to you is: First of all, do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's wise to go into private session at this point

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Thank you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My question to you is: I'm going to take you back to the time that the shooting started on April the 21st, 21 April, 1992. And I believe you testified earlier that the shooting started after 6.00. I believe in your testimony that you said both sides started shooting. What did you mean by that when you said "both sides started shooting"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thought that these opened fire and those others, I mean these ones attacked and those returned. I mean, what else could it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: From where you were at you could hear people in town firing back -- firing back; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Now, you had sent your family away and you stayed; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Why is it that you stayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Should I say that? Because of my work. I had to go to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you know if, prior to the time that the shooting started, whether any Muslims, any Bosniaks, had gone so far as to acquire weapons to defend themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were poorly armed. Some bought, some had their hunting rifles from before. And it was just a few but only people had to go to be evacuated, so as not to fall victims to --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You said that there were some people and that they were poorly armed. Some had their hunting rifles from before. How many civilians did you know were armed in Bosanska Krupa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult it say. I didn't count. I can't really know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Roughly. An approximate figure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What time? No, about five, six hunting rifles in the area of the town where I was. Elsewhere, I don't know. I really don't know. How can I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fair. Two real quick questions about this area. Were you aware of any troops that came in from Bihac to assist in the defence of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did hear something about it but I don't really know all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: What did you hear about it, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that some had come. I don't know where from. That they had come from the Cazin area or somewhere, and that they came, I don't know how many of them, well, no, no, I don't really know. I'm telling you I didn't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fine. Did you know whether or not any members of the patriotic league were in Bosanska Krupa at the time that the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then, yes, but once again, I'm not really familiar with that, since I had nothing to do with it, I wasn't involved in that so I don't really know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And that leads to my next question: Were you involved in the resistance? Did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't part of it, but I had a pistol and I had a licence for it, because that was the kind of job I did. That job required that I have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My recollection is that you were in a basement when you were discovered by the soldiers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When the soldiers found you, did you have a -- that pistol or any other weapon nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had that pistol and I was the only one who had anything. All the others had nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Was that pistol loaded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Loaded but not a single bullet was fired. Those who took it saw it. Naturally, I didn't offer any resistance. I simply had taken shelter in a basement not to be killed or wounded, but then as we were trying to cross to the other side, they just came up and we were caught.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Right. And after you were caught, you were sent to the school and there was some sort of court that was set up in a building right near the school; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already testified on this so go straight to what you want from him, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the witness please come back to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, everywhere but that was in Jasenica taken to the school in Jasenica and that's where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: As His Honour has reminded me, let me get straight to this question. While were you in this court process, were they dividing the people in custody into civilian prisoners, military prisoners or any other groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They separated us people, they were sending allegedly, well, no, they were all civilians. I don't know. Some allegedly cooperated with the town defence or something, and they kept those and those they didn't they sent them on, they sent them to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Were the people that you were kept with, were those the people that assisted in the town's defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Who? What? What men?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think you told us that when you were in detention at the school, that you were in a room and you shared that room with other men. Were those other men that you shared that room with at the school, were those men that had assisted in the town's defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. I want to talk to you about a few selected events that happened while you were in custody. During the course of your testimony, you told us about various individuals that were taken up on a hill to do labour, and then you described how, I believe, the number was five of those men, were killed while working on the hill. Do you remember testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, but three were killed on the hill and two were killed in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My question to you is this: First of all with respect to the three killings on the hill, were you personally present when they were killed? Did you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked there together but those they wanted to kill --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you see any of those three killings yourself? Did you witness personally any of those three killings on the hill? Answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Again, yes or no, did you personally witness, personally see, the two other killings that you say happened at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Oh, in the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The two other killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which I think we better specify which school here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I don't know if this is something I need to go into private session or not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think you need to go into private session but whether it's the Petar Kocic school or whether you're referring to the Jasenica school. Or the school at Jasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm talking about Petar Kocic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you witness any of the killings that took place there?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can assist, Your Honour, I think you're referring to the Suad Sefic and --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The gentleman who had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Mirsad Budimlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you see any of those two being killed with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean Sefic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one is Sefic, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sefic was poisoned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And Mirsad Budimlic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm almost done, you're doing very, just bear with me a little longer. The second-to-last area that I want to ask you about has to deal with the killing of 11 people at the Petar Kocic school by someone that was -- his name was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Jojo Plavanjac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Here is my question to you on this and it's very simple: Do you remember anyone saying anything to the man with the gun who did the shooting before the shooting actually occurred? Did anyone try to stop him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, allegedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard Zdravko, the policeman who was on duty, the guard there. He was saying, "Jojo, don't do this. Jojo, don't." Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 17515 to 17527.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Finally, in your statement, you tell us that there were two times that prisoner exchanges were set, and two times that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You almost made it but then they called you back at the last minute. Do you know why the first two times you weren't exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT56 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The commander, Momo, was there, and various questions were put and then later, he said, "I made a mistake for having stopped you, for not having carried the exchange through."

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. That's all the questions I have, sir. I wish you a safe journey home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Is there a re-examination, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any questions? Yes, sir, look at me. We have come to an end. That's the end of your testimony here. And you will be now escorted out of this courtroom by the usher. We are taking the usual precautions to make sure that on your way out, no one will be able to see you, as you see he's drawing the curtains down. On behalf of the Tribunal, but particularly on behalf of myself and Judge Janu and Judge Taya, who together with me compose this Trial Chamber, I should like to thank you for having come over here to give testimony. The only thing which remains for me before I see you out of this courtroom is to wish you, joining together with the others, wishing you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova is taking the next witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, the next witness, Madam Richterova, I know he's got a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes the following witness has the same protective measures, pseudonym and facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Just to use the time before the witness will be brought, I want to inform you that I am going to tender into evidence the two statements, attachments and the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That's perfect. I just wanted to make sure that we have -- we are talking of the same documents. According to what I have, he gave a statement to the Prosecution on the 27th of August of 1999. Is that correct? And the ERN number is 00 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct, 27 of August, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. 00844657 is the ERN number for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
